articles.title: Daybreak Red is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
articles.description: Daybreak Red brings GPT-5.6 Cyber to approved customers in AWS GovCloud (US-East) through Amazon Bedrock for authorized cybersecurity work.
articles.full_text:
Title: Daybreak Red is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East)

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/daybreak-red-aws-govcloud

Final URL: https://openai.com/index/daybreak-red-aws-govcloud/

Markdown Content:
Building on the availability of Daybreak models on Amazon Bedrock, GPT‑5.6 Cyber is now available to approved customers [in AWS GovCloud (US-East)⁠(opens in a new window)](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/10/openai-daybreak-red-govcloud-east/) through Daybreak Red. This expansion gives government security teams a new way to apply advanced cybersecurity capabilities within the AWS environments they use to support critical missions.

Daybreak Red provides access to OpenAI’s purpose-trained cybersecurity models for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing. GPT‑5.6 Cyber can help defenders investigate complex software weaknesses, reproduce vulnerabilities in controlled settings, and develop mitigations. Qualified security practitioners should review findings and proposed fixes before implementation.

## Bringing frontier cybersecurity capabilities to government teams

For government organizations, adopting advanced cybersecurity capabilities requires more than model performance. Teams also need to work within established security, governance, and operational requirements.

Availability in AWS GovCloud (US-East) gives eligible teams a path to incorporate GPT‑5.6 Cyber into those workflows through Amazon Bedrock. Defenders can use it to reason through security findings, assess their impact, and evaluate fixes, helping connect vulnerability research to practical improvements in defense.

Daybreak Red gives verified defenders greater latitude for authorized cybersecurity work, with fewer refusals for these tasks alongside stronger identity verification, monitoring, and access controls.

For Daybreak Red on Amazon Bedrock, inference data is not used to train models, and customers do not need to share their Daybreak Red data with OpenAI.

## Get started

Access requires OpenAI Daybreak Red approval and AWS provisioning. To get started, complete the [Daybreak application](https://openai.com/form/enterprise-trusted-access-for-cyber/) or contact your OpenAI or AWS account team about eligibility. Once approved, work with your AWS account team to enable access. Daybreak Red approval does not automatically enable model access on AWS.

articles.title: Introducing Images 2.6
articles.description: Images 2.6 brings faster image generation, GIF creation, more precise editing, and new API controls across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API.
articles.full_text:
Title: Introducing Images 2.6

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/introducing-images-2-6

Final URL: https://openai.com/index/introducing-images-2-6/

Markdown Content:
We’re introducing Images 2.6 in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, bringing your ideas to life faster. With this, you can bring motion to your images with GIFs — from animating a brand mascot or character to turning a product shot into an eye-catching loop. You can also create polished visuals faster and refine them with greater precision — keeping characters, products, and brand details consistent as you edit.

People around the world now create 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. On average, that’s more than half a billion images created per day.

A montage of animated scenes generated with Images 2.6.

## Faster iteration and more professional visuals

Images 2.6 generates images 50% faster than before. In the API, we offer GPT‑Image‑2.6 Flare and Sunburst for developers to choose from. When quality is set to low, Flare can generate images in as little as six seconds. For work that calls for greater detail and precision, GPT‑Image‑2.6 Sunburst brings higher-quality image generation and even greater image consistency across edits when quality is set to medium or high. Flare also improves layout quality for posters, product imagery, and other professional visuals.

Side-by-side image-generation latency comparison using a luxury travel advertisement, with generation timers shown at eight-times playback speed.

## Animate your ideas with GIFs

For moments that call for motion, GIFs bring another dimension to your ideas. Marketers and creators can animate a brand mascot for a campaign, create reactions and memes for social media, or use animated storyboards to explore character movement before video production.

A chibi office worker reacts to a falling stock-market chart.

_Created by OpenArt_

**Prompt 1****:** Create a single animation sprite sheet for a seamless looping GIF. A super-cute chibi adult office worker sits at a desk watching a computer monitor with a clearly plunging stock-market line chart. The sequence: hopeful expression, notices the chart falling, eyes widen, face crumples, large cartoon tears stream down both cheeks, then quietly wipes tears while still staring at the falling chart. Oversized round head, tiny body, big expressive eyes, soft rounded features, messy fluffy hair, white shirt and loosened tie. Exactly 6 sequential frames arranged in a precise 3-column by 2-row grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Every panel has identical dimensions. Fixed front three-quarter camera, same character, same desk, monitor, outfit, and cozy miniature office background. Clear incremental facial and tear motion; sixth frame transitions smoothly toward the first. Polished kawaii chibi 3D toy-like style, warm pastel lighting, funny and sympathetic mood. No captions, no words, no numbers, no logos, no speech bubbles, no panel labels, no borders, no gutters.

A chibi office worker celebrates a rising stock-market chart.

_Created by OpenArt_

**Prompt 2:**Create a single animation sprite sheet for a seamless looping GIF. A super-cute chibi adult office worker sits at a desk watching a computer monitor with a clearly soaring stock-market line chart and a large upward arrow. The sequence: notices the chart rising, eyes widen with delight, jumps up cheering, grabs a handful of generic paper banknotes with no readable currency markings, then happily tosses the banknotes into the air like confetti while laughing. Oversized round head, tiny body, big sparkling expressive eyes, soft rounded features, messy fluffy hair, white shirt and loosened tie. Exactly 6 sequential frames arranged in a precise 3-column by 2-row grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Every panel has identical dimensions. Fixed front three-quarter camera, same character, desk, monitor, outfit, and cozy miniature office background. Clear incremental body, arm, and flying-paper motion; sixth frame transitions smoothly toward the first. Polished kawaii chibi 3D toy-like style, bright celebratory pastel lighting, funny joyful mood. No captions, no words, no numbers, no logos, no real currency symbols, no speech bubbles, no panel labels, no borders, no gutters.

And you don’t need a polished design to get started — even a simple sketch can become an expressive, animated character for videos, games, and more.

![Image 1: An owl drawn in pen on lined paper.](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/7xC8whl4xN2cOTxQSLMfQ8/60b25185d53ca63f000341f0acbfba7a/owl-sketch-square.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

An animated owl created from the hand-drawn sketch.

From personal reactions to brand mascots and product visuals, GIFs give people and businesses a playful way to communicate. Town, a startup building an AI work assistant, used Images 2.6 in the API to explore how animated characters could bring more personality to everyday interactions at work.

Monty, an animated character in the Town work assistant, appears above the message box as a typing indicator.

## More ways to create and edit in the API

A presenter at a laptop in the image-editing demonstration.

With Images 2.6, developers get more control over how images are created, edited, and carried into the next stage of a project. Image markup, already available in ChatGPT, comes to the API so teams can pinpoint exactly where to make specific changes. SVG exports make designs ready to use across websites, apps, and print.

A new complexity parameter lets developers adjust how much planning the model does to meet a request, with lower settings suited to quick edits. Image quality controls visual detail and fidelity, while complexity guides how much goes into the scene.

For most editing tasks, we recommend low complexity for faster edits, paired with the image quality your workflow requires. For scenes with many elements or constraints, try medium or high complexity effort.

See what early access customers generated using Images 2.6:

![Image 2: A giant multicolored glass whale floats above misty mountains beside a stone chapel at sunset.](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/5g2ztPz3EqktNQwQWa7Al8/d42c517c10fcbcb3c0da00bd5fe6b26e/picsart-glass-whale.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

## Pricing and availability

Images 2.6 is available globally today in ChatGPT and Codex across all subscription tiers on desktop, mobile, and web.

GPT‑Image‑2.6 Sunburst and GPT‑Image‑2.6 Flare are available in the API. See[pricing details here.⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing#image-generation)

Learn more about our safety evaluations and safeguards for Images 2.6 in the [system card⁠(opens in a new window)](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/chatgpt-images-2-6).

articles.title: DevRev delivers autonomous self-service with GPT-6.1 Sol
articles.description: DevRev uses GPT-6.1 Sol to power Computer and Operator, balancing reasoning, speed, and cost for enterprise service.
articles.full_text:
Title: DevRev delivers autonomous self-service with GPT-6.1 Sol

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/devrev-enterprise-self-service

Final URL: https://openai.com/index/devrev-enterprise-self-service/

Markdown Content:
[DevRev⁠(opens in a new window)](https://devrev.ai/) built Computer and Operator to help service and operations teams carry even the hardest customer and employee requests through to completion. Computer and Operator are designed to reason across live data. Actions are reversible, and answers point back to their sources, explains Ahmed Bashir, DevRev’s chief technology officer.

DevRev combines OpenAI models, including GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol, with its harness for connecting company knowledge and giving teams control over the actions an agent can take. DevRev sees OpenAI models as providing reasoning and reliability with the speed and cost of serving customers and employees.

> _“It’s a combination of being able to have the right reasoning capabilities, being able to be trusted, highly aligned, and most importantly, it has to work from a latency perspective.”_

—Ahmed Bashir, Chief Technology Officer, DevRev

## Making AI work with company context

OpenAI models power the reasoning, planning, and tool selection behind both Computer and Operator. In DevRev’s Agent Studio, users can describe how they want a tool to behave in a conversation with AI and define parts of its behavior with fixed rules.

DevRev tests the models together with the software that supplies company context, enforces permissions, and controls actions. Its Enterprise-Bench benchmark evaluates how well they work when data has multiple versions, information sits in different systems, and access depends on a person’s role.

Ahmed says GPT‑6.1 Sol performs well in those evaluations. When a customer or employee is interacting with an AI agent, the model needs to understand the nuances of the request and respond quickly, at a cost the business can sustain. “I think it strikes the balance perfectly,” Ahmed says.

## Building software and sales demos with Codex

Inside DevRev, engineers have made a clear choice about the best way to build. “Our entire team uses Codex,” Ahmed says. The adoption grew organically after engineers explored multiple coding tools. By the time of the interview, DevRev had moved fully to Codex and dropped its Cursor licenses.

For Ahmed, this reflects what developers value: “Developers are really just looking for the best tool, and you can’t fool them.” His engineers were unequivocal about wanting to continue with Codex.

> _“We think that Codex is far and away the best experience.”_

—Ahmed Bashir, Chief Technology Officer, DevRev

DevRev’s sales engineers also use GPT‑6 Astra to create demos for the company’s booths at international conferences.

## Responding faster to customers and employees

When a customer or employee asks for help, the request may require Operator to understand the issue, take approved action, or route to Computer to prepare the right person to act. Ahmed sees opportunities for the Decisions API and Ultrafast to help those workflows finish quickly, without requiring deep reasoning at every step.

Some of those decisions are difficult and expensive to define with fixed rules, especially when the information they depend on keeps changing. Ahmed wants builders to be able to describe more of that logic conversationally and choose the right kind of intelligence for each task. “These things have to be able to run and complete themselves in seconds, not minutes,” he says.

## Realizing the promise of self-service

DevRev’s next ambition is for Operator to take on longer, more demanding customer and employee requests while keeping actions traceable, permissioned, and reversible.

Ahmed sees familiar support tasks, such as finding a knowledge-base answer, upgrading a plan, or getting a refund, as only the beginning. “We want to really realize that promise of self-service,” he says.

With OpenAI’s frontier intelligence, DevRev is building toward Computer and Operator carrying more complex requests through to resolution, with the company knowledge and controls to act on a person’s behalf.

articles.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world
articles.description: Discover how ChatGPT and Codex are helping engineers accelerate CAD, PCB design, simulation, and other workflows across the physical world.
articles.full_text:
Title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/accelerating-engineering-for-the-physical-world

Final URL: https://openai.com/index/accelerating-engineering-for-the-physical-world/

Markdown Content:
Today, we’re sharing advances in how OpenAI models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products. These capabilities span mechanical and electrical engineering and end-to-end system design, and are already helping our internal teams test ideas and iterate faster.

Across these projects, engineers need to bring together mechanical designs, electronics, software, and manufacturing requirements using specialized tools. We’re teaching models to support that work, from preparing drawings and setting up simulations to coordinating changes across disciplines. Our goal is to give engineers more time to explore ideas and improve designs.

Over the past year, improved frontier model capabilities have helped our internal teams test new ideas and iterate faster, and we are seeing early evidence of these capabilities improving professional workflows in industry as well. We’re working with collaborators to understand where these capabilities can make the biggest difference and what needs to improve. If you’re an engineer, engineering firm, or software vendor involved in the design, simulation, manufacturing, or production of complex physical products, we’d love to [work with you](https://openai.com/form/computer-use-research-collaboration/) to shape this effort around the tools you use and the problems you need to solve.

## Designing a device with Astra

We tested[Astra’s state-of-the-art performance⁠](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/) in multimodal and computer use workflows by seeing if we can create a device without any direct human edits. To do this, we used GPT‑6 to define the functional requirements and design the enclosure, printed circuit board (PCB), and software integrations needed to create a device users can use to talk to Codex.

*   **Aesthetics and design:**Astra developed the look of the device, drawing on our recent [Work Louder⁠(opens in a new window)](https://worklouder.cc/codex-micro) collaboration and references from games and toys.

*   **Mechanical design:**Astra designed the [enclosure⁠(opens in a new window)](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/5aP4AhwHhDUmDxisSLcb2X/12114476f73d643b73dffe90b819cc0c/prototype-device-enclosure-diagram.png) and the internal structures that hold the components in place.

*   **Electrical design:**Astra selected the electrical components and designed the printed circuit board (PCB), including component placement and connections, to fit within the enclosure.

*   **UI/UX and software:**Astra designed the user interface and generated the firmware and software integrations needed to connect the device to Codex.

Two team members designed this test device with Astra in under a week while working on it as a side project. A contract manufacturer built a small batch of prototypes in under a month.

Getting the device ready for manufacturing still required several rounds of review and iteration. Astra did not consistently account for the manufacturer’s production limits, tolerances, or details required for assembly. These gaps are helping us identify what future models need to do better.

## Accelerating OpenAI hardware teams

OpenAI’s hardware and infrastructure teams use Codex and ChatGPT to create and revise computer-aided design (CAD) models, prepare manufacturing drawings, set up simulations, and review designs. This work spans robotics and compute infrastructure. Since February, model usage across our hardware teams, measured in tokens, has grown 23-fold.

1 of 3

## Measuring progress on engineering tasks

We’re also measuring progress in newer models on tasks that combine coding with engineering knowledge. BenchCAD 2.0 tests whether models can reconstruct 3D parts and assemblies and identify connections in circuit boards. A newer internal model achieved an average score of 0.875, compared with 0.594 for GPT‑6 Astra at its highest reasoning setting. While the engineering lifecycle includes many other elements beyond design, we view improvements in capability here as early evidence of the ability of AI models to positively impact iteration speed for professional workflows.

## Safely deploying with industry collaborators

We’re working with a small group of industry collaborators to test these capabilities on real engineering problems. Their engineers review model outputs for accuracy and practical use, helping us understand which tasks models can support today and what needs to be improved for safe and reliable use.

We’re expanding our collaboration with [Chip Ganassi Racing](https://openai.com/index/chip-ganassi-racing/) (CGR) to explore how OpenAI models can accelerate engineering and prototyping. Working with its R&D team, we’re testing workflows that turn 3D scans of existing parts into editable CAD models and 2D manufacturing drawings. This is particularly useful when the original design files are unavailable.

CGR engineers review the models and drawings for accuracy and manufacturability. Their feedback helps us identify where models can reduce manual work and where further improvements are needed.

We’re also announcing a new research collaboration with Mazda. Our research and Forward Deployed Engineering teams are working with Mazda’s aerodynamics and crash-safety engineers to explore how OpenAI models can help develop and evaluate new vehicle designs.

The work uses simulations of airflow and structural behavior to explore improvements in performance while accounting for styling and cost. We’ll share more progress and results in the coming months.

GPT‑6 Astra helps Mazda’s aerodynamics engineers explore ways to reduce vehicle drag by modeling new nose shapes, simulating airflow, and refining the most promising designs. Agreement for use has been obtained from Mazda Motor Corporation. Any republication or reuse elsewhere is strictly prohibited.

## Help shape AI for engineering and manufacturing

We have been working closely with industry partners and early adopters to push the bounds of what we can do with AI agents in hardware and manufacturing. These early results have shown exciting promise, and we’re now looking for collaborators to accelerate these capability improvements and ensure we deploy these safely into industry.

If you are interested in working with us to shape the training and development of our frontier models by identifying high-value use cases, software tooling, or future opportunities in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, electromechanical design, mechatronics, or a related field, please fill out [this form](https://openai.com/form/computer-use-research-collaboration/) and we'll be in touch.

articles.title: How Cisco defends at machine speed with OpenAI
articles.description: Cisco combines network intelligence with OpenAI models to strengthen enterprise security. Learn how it is building more adaptive defenses.
articles.full_text:
Title: How Cisco defends at machine speed with OpenAI

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/cisco-cyber

Final URL: https://openai.com/index/cisco-cyber/

Markdown Content:
Cisco builds the networking and security infrastructure that organizations rely on to connect and protect their systems. As adversaries leverage AI to scale automated attacks and craft exploits at machine-speed, defending enterprise infrastructure must evolve. Pairing Cisco’s vast network telemetry with frontier AI reasoning gives defenders the toolkit necessary to outpace emerging threats. OpenAI’s rigorous approach to enterprise data privacy—centered on zero data retention, strict customer data boundaries, and verifiable isolation—means Cisco could confidently deploy frontier intelligence across mission-critical systems without compromising customer priorities or sensitive telemetry.

## Connecting network intelligence for stronger defense

Cisco’s defense starts where threats move: the network. Patel describes a shift from a single security perimeter to controls distributed across microservices, containers, and clusters. “We can put a mini security stack in front of every microservice, every Kubernetes container, and every Kubernetes cluster, and fuse security into the fabric of the network,” he says.

Controls at the application level can restrict communication to the connections each service needs, reducing the paths an attacker can use to spread. Security teams can also isolate affected systems more selectively, allowing unaffected services to keep running while they investigate and respond.

Combining that network intelligence with OpenAI’s models allows Cisco to correlate signals at machine scale, Patel says. “Two signals might seem benign in isolation, but together they can reveal a meaningful pattern. Network intelligence allows us to correlate data across the network and derive insights to inform secure operations.”

Patel points to a pressing challenge for defenders: the gap between how quickly attackers can exploit a vulnerability and how long organizations take to patch it. He sees AI as a way to help narrow that gap, giving defenders the capacity to investigate more threats and respond faster. “AI hands attackers speed and scale. Using AI for defense is a prerequisite for staying safe,” he says.

He describes initiatives like Daybreak and GPT‑6 Astra as advances that strengthen security for both Cisco and its customers. “We’re able to find and patch vulnerabilities more efficiently, while shortening the time needed for investigation, response, and remediation,” Patel says.

> “Daybreak and GPT-6 Astra have been step function improvements, not just for our security posture, but for our customers’ security posture.”

—Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer at Cisco

Patel sees a path to adoption that builds on the processes teams already use to find and address vulnerabilities. “These capabilities can fit into your existing scanning workflows, so you don’t have to fundamentally change how your team works.”

## Rethinking security for an agentic world

As agents become more autonomous, security teams also need to distinguish malicious interference from an agent pursuing a legitimate goal in an unintended way. Patel says that requires security telemetry alongside observability data, so teams can assess both threats and agent behavior.

He outlines three priorities: protect agents from malicious attacks, detect and intercept unintended behavior, and operate in near real time. These priorities are guiding the shift towards policies and controls that can adapt as agents act.

Through the Daybreak Defense Network, Cisco and OpenAI are exploring how to help security teams triage exposure faster and enforce the right controls in Cisco Cloud Control. For Patel, that can help shift the advantage back to defenders.

> “OpenAI is shifting the advantage to defenders by allowing us to operate at machine speed and scale.”

—Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer at Cisco

articles.title: Heimstaden is changing residential real estate management with AI
articles.description: Discover how Heimstaden uses OpenAI’s ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to transform property management, cut costs, and empower employees across Europe.
articles.full_text:
Title: Heimstaden is changing residential real estate management with AI

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/heimstaden

Final URL: https://openai.com/index/heimstaden/

Markdown Content:
## The buildings haven’t changed. Everything around them has.

A hundred years ago, managing a residential building meant finding tenants, collecting rent and keeping properties in good condition. Today, these fundamentals remain remarkably similar. What is changing is _how_ that work gets done.

For European residential real estate operator[**Heimstaden**⁠(opens in a new window)](https://heimstaden.com/), this presents an opportunity: what if AI could fundamentally change how thousands of homes are managed?

In June 2025, Heimstaden’s leadership decided to accelerate its bet on AI. After evaluating several platforms, the company chose OpenAI. The goal was twofold; empower employees and rethink the processes at the heart of its business.

The ambition is to move towards increasingly self-operating buildings, where AI can help anticipate needs, coordinate work and support decisions across the property lifecycle. “The purpose of our buildings hasn’t changed.” says Helge Krogsbøl, Co-CEO at Heimstaden. “We provide homes for people. But the way we operate them continues to change as we challenge conventions and adopt new technology.”

> _**“We see AI as one of the biggest opportunities to accelerate that transformation.”**_

—Helge Krogsbøl, Co-CEO, Heimstaden

## Reimagining the business of letting homes

Consider what happens when a property becomes vacant.

Traditionally, getting it back onto the market involves assessing rental value, arranging photography, producing advertisements and responding to market demand. Each stage requires time, coordination and specialist input. And it is an information challenge; understanding what you own, what the competition has, and what the customer wants.

AI is now supporting all the key steps in this process:

*   **Pricing:**Intelligence and recommendations based on tools built in ChatGPT Sites

*   **Advertising:**Image styling and apartment descriptions done by AI

*   **Review listings:**Agent reviews all live ads against Heimstaden’s quality standards

*   **Feedback:**AI generated market feedback helps letting teams take corrective action which makes prices increasingly dynamic

Employees remain responsible for reviewing and approving decisions. But the work surrounding those decisions is changing.

In the Netherlands, the cost of producing a virtually staged property image has fallen from approximately €50 to less than €0.10 which is a reduction of more than 99%. Heimstaden estimates annual savings potential of €130,000 in that market alone.

The significance extends beyond cheaper advertisements. By applying AI across the letting process, Heimstaden is building a more responsive way to bring homes to market.

“Our AI strategy is based on three pillars.” says Nikolaj Brammer, Heimstaden’s Chief Digital Officer, “First, we empower employees through training and access to the right tools. Second, we have a central transformation office and a network of AI champions to drive larger AI initiatives. Third, we strengthen the foundations by making our property management systems and data models ready for AI.”

Letting puts all three pillars into practice: tools and training enable colleagues to create virtually staged images and listings; our central team coordinates improvements across pricing, advertising, ad review and market feedback; and we are making property data accessible to the AI tools that support pricing and listing creation.

> _**“We started by breaking down our most important business processes and asking where AI could create value. Letting is a good example: it’s not about automating one task, but improving how the whole process works.”**_

—Nikolaj Brammer, Chief Digital Officer, Heimstaden

## When domain experts become builders

Some of the most significant changes are happening far from traditional software engineering teams.

Heimstaden needed to assess environmental risks across its portfolio. The information existed, but was scattered across public sources, formats and datasets. Turning it into a usable assessment would have required substantial manual work and technical resources.

Heimstaden’s Julia Erlandsen, an environmental sustainability analyst without a software development background, used Codex to help build a different approach.

Codex supported the discovery, cleaning and standardisation of data, quality checking and the development of repeatable processing pipelines. Julia retained control over the methodology and validation.

The result: 20,112 assets assessed, more than six million rows of useful data generated, and an estimated delivery requirement reduced from five people working for a year to two people working for two months.

Heimstaden also avoided engaging external consultants which would otherwise have been needed to solve the problem.

What began as a complex analytical project is becoming a repeatable capability, supporting climate-risk assessments, reporting requirements and investor decision-making.

> _**“Codex helped us build a solution that would previously have required substantial technical support. We now own the methodology and can continue developing it ourselves.”**_

—Julia Erlandsen, Environmental Sustainability Analyst, Heimstaden

## Responsible AI adoption

Heimstaden’s AI adoption focuses on tasks employees need help with. After ChatGPT Enterprise launched in September 2025, half of employees were using it within two to three months. A central AI transformation office maintains a library of use cases so colleagues can learn from examples across the business.

Employees use approved tools within rules for data security. They remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated content before sending it and for approving decisions.

Adoption extends to real estate caretakers, including some who were initially sceptical. In Norway, one caretaker used ChatGPT to assess a neglected apartment and draft a prioritised refurbishment plan, turning observations into a structured plan they could review and refine.

> _**“People across the business are finding practical ways to use AI in their daily work. Our job is to scale what works while keeping data secure, responsibilities clear and people in control.”**_

—Andreas Kalmar Lindquist, Manager AI First Team Heimstaden

## The next frontier: From answering questions to taking action

Heimstaden is already preparing for the next stage: AI that can work across systems and coordinate multi-step processes.

Its Procurement Intelligence Platform, currently being rolled out, combines workflow automation with OpenAI models accessed through APIs. Designed to operate across Outlook, SharePoint and Teams, it supports contract analysis, negotiation preparation and contract lifecycle management, with employees retaining responsibility for commercial decisions and approvals.

The longer-term ambition is more fundamental.

Heimstaden is co-developing Amplio Estate, a modern property management system designed to support AI-powered workflows through MCP. The goal is to enable employees to use AI, such as ChatGPT, to retrieve property information and take action in core business systems, with appropriate human oversight.

This is how Heimstaden begins turning the idea of self-operating buildings into a practical technology roadmap.

## Results at a glance

*   **More than 99% lower image production costs** in the Netherlands.

*   **20,112 property assets assessed with Codex**, reducing the estimated delivery requirement from five people over one year to two people over two months.

*   **50% employee adoption within 2–3 months** of rollout.

## Leadership lessons:

*   **Focus on people:**Adoption and imagination are the bottlenecks (not tech)

*   **Find your champions:**The biggest returns come from colleagues driving change locally

*   **Get the process right:**AI will not fix a broken process, but it can dramatically scale a good one.

## What’s next

Heimstaden’s vision is not of buildings without people, but of properties supported by increasingly intelligent systems which will improve decision making for employees and increase ability to resolve matters for customers.

The buildings will remain much as they have always been—homes and roofs over people’s heads. The way they’re operated has forever changed.

[View more](https://www.anthropic.com/search?topic=life-sciences)

_Anthropic’s [life sciences team](https://www.anthropic.com/science) is working to accelerate curing disease. Over the past several months, our scientists have engaged in deep research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines: [BigHat Biosciences](https://www.bighatbio.com/), [Bristol Myers Squibb](https://www.bms.com/), [Divergence Labs](https://divergencelabs.com/), [Enveda](https://enveda.com/), [Generate Biomedicines](https://generatebiomedicines.com/), and [The Column Group](https://www.thecolumngroup.com/). We've also begun drug discovery efforts of our own. In doing so, we've learned a lot about how Claude can support drug development, and how we’ll need to improve Claude further to realize AI's potential in medicine. We plan to scale this work up substantially from here_.

There are many opportunities to speed up drug development, even beyond the most commonly discussed applications of AI, like [proposing initial designs](https://www.anthropic.com/research/Claude-accelerates-protein-design) for new molecules. Developing a drug involves many varied tasks: doing early research to identify a target for a drug and the right type of drug to engage it, designing a molecule with the right properties, optimizing it to be manufactured reliably at scale, drafting the regulatory filings needed to run clinical trials, designing and administering those trials, and much more.

Our strategy to realize AI’s medical benefits is based on having AI increasingly involved in all of these tasks. There is no single problem to solve; the bottlenecks are distributed all throughout the drug development process. The best way to identify and work through these bottlenecks is to get deeply involved in real drug programs, across many different disease areas and stages of development.

So, over the past several months, we’ve partnered with six organizations to do so. We’ve also started drug discovery efforts of our own, including programs for rare childhood forms of muscular dystrophy, where Claude handles much of the scientific and operational work.

This work serves our goals in three ways. First, it lets us better understand the strengths and limitations of our models in relation to a much wider range of drug development tasks (we’ve already prioritized specific improvements to our models based on what we’ve learned so far). Second, these programs can serve as case studies for the wider life sciences community. If Claude is to significantly increase the rate of new cures, we need to work with many more biotechnology firms and integrate Claude more deeply into their development processes. Third, these projects should, if their positive trajectories continue, have direct impact themselves. We’re optimistic that some may result in effective new medicines for the diseases they target, including food allergies, rare childhood diseases, and several forms of cancer.

In this post, we provide an update on our progress with our partners, along with technical reports that describe our thought process, methods, and early results in more detail. We then briefly outline where our work is headed next.

## Case studies

**Generate Biomedicines: modality engineering.** Generate Biomedicines has been working on increasing the usefulness of a cancer treatment known as CAR T-cell therapy. This therapy has historically helped treat blood cell cancers; Generate aims to reengineer it so that it can treat solid tumor cancers too. To do this, they’re aiming to shorten one part of the therapy’s genetic instructions, which would create room for additional instructions suited to other kinds of cancer. Six Generate scientists used Claude Code to propose new designs for this part. One design was about 70% shorter than the standard version, and in lab tests it was more effective: it allowed immune cells to make roughly 10 times as many receptors (the proteins they use to spot cancer cells), it killed tumor cells more efficiently, and the immune cells remained active for longer. Read more, and see [Generate’s technical report](https://generatebiomedicines.com/publications/refactored-intracellular-domains-enhance-car-expression-and-function/).

**Divergence Labs: hit generation.** Divergence Labs is working on a novel way to treat food allergies. Food allergies are set off by a reaction from a molecule called IgE, some of which is attached to our immune cells and some of which floats freely in our blood. Divergence Labs is developing drugs that would detach the IgE from our immune cells entirely, rather than solely neutralizing the IgE circulating in our blood, as standard medications do. This could provide a much more effective treatment, but it requires a precise design, with two “arms”: one that would bind tightly to IgE, and another that would help prise IgE from the immune cell. Claude converted Divergence Labs’ goals into a detailed design plan, and then, largely autonomously, generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month to be narrowed down and tested. In those early tests, Divergence found “hits” for both arms: three designs that could bind to IgE, and 20 that could dislodge it. Three of those 20 appeared to dislodge IgE more than the standard medication. Its next step is to build a drug that combines the two arms. Read more, and see [Divergence’s technical report](https://divergencelabs.com/publications/ige-preprint.pdf).

**BigHat Biosciences: lead optimization.** BigHat Biosciences pairs AI with an automated lab to improve potential drugs (or “leads”), which must bind their target tightly, remain stable through manufacturing and storage, and avoid clumping together (among other criteria). BigHat’s scientists and an Anthropic researcher worked with Claude to improve these three properties in two leads, both antibody fragments that could become parts of future drugs: one designed to target cancer cells, and one designed to keep a drug in the body longer. Claude, connected to BigHat’s lab data system, Reccy, proposed changes to each molecule, and BigHat’s lab made and tested about 1,010 variants in about 10 weeks. Partway through, the team suspected the standard heat-stability and clumping metrics were misleading. Claude and the researcher reanalyzed the raw data, then proposed different metrics and a protocol change to test them. BigHat’s scientists refined and ran it, and the main predictions held. Compared with the originals, the best versions bound more than 10x more tightly, the cancer-targeting lead stayed in solution 18°C higher, and the lead for longer-lasting drugs clumped more than 100x more slowly. Read more, and see [BigHat’s technical report](https://www.bighatbio.com/bighat-anthropic-collaboration-report-10-27-2026).

**Enveda: manufacturing and filings.** To conduct clinical trials, companies need records showing that each batch of a new drug has been made to strict quality standards, and to submit an application to regulators, among other requirements. At Enveda, manufacturing chemists spent up to 75% of their time on paperwork. To ease the load, Enveda built a system that connects all of its manufacturing documents to Claude, then lets Claude flag any possible issues. Over tests on 1,061 pages of documentation, Claude caught all 11 issues that human reviewers had spotted—and flagged seven they’d missed. In the process, this method reduced human review time by 89%, from over 25 hours to less than three. Separately, Claude wrote the first drafts of two important regulatory documents. One took four hours, compared to about three months by hand. For the other, Enveda’s standard human review process found one minor error. Read more, and see [Enveda’s technical report](https://enveda.com/CMC-Document-Processor/).

**The Column Group (TCG): company creation.** Because drug discovery can be slow, expensive, and prone to failure, investors in biotechnology companies have favored safer, previously validated ideas over riskier new ones, even when the latter could help more patients. We’ve been working with TCG to see whether Claude can change this by cutting the time and cost of drug discovery so that investors can confidently support more ambitious ideas. Specifically, TCG is establishing Pleiades, a new company that will use Claude to run many more—and more complex—drug programs than is usual for a small team. This could be a model for how Claude can reduce both the scientific and the operational and administrative overhead required to run a biotechnology company. If this works, this model could be replicated across the industry and direct investment toward harder problems in medicine. Pleiades is currently developing new tools and workflows for Claude; its very first Claude skill, which helps Claude assess whether drug targets are worth pursuing, has been evaluated on 45 target-disease pairs. Read more.

More recently, we’ve also begun working with [Bristol Myers Squibb](https://www.bms.com/) (BMS) to find and address bottlenecks in clinical trial planning. BMS is using Claude to assess plans of an early-stage drug in clinical trials, and to estimate the likelihood of those trials succeeding. Together, we plan to expand this work in 2027 to understand its potential for increasing the probability of success in early development.

> _“We use Claude at the clinical trial stage to analyze proprietary data, create a clinical study plan, and weigh the study’s chance of success. From a single prompt, Claude generated a robust initial analysis that helped inform our assessment of different development options, which would otherwise take days to complete. We did all of this while ensuring the security of our highly sensitive data. We look forward to expanding this work across our pipeline to support portfolio-level decisions.”_

_**Michael Pourdehnad, MD**, Senior Vice President, Head of Early Clinical Development, Hematology, Oncology and Cell Therapy._

In addition to our work with these partners, we’ve begun to run some research programs ourselves. We’ve acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person company that has been developing treatments for two rare forms of muscular dystrophy. Its founder, Cody Tranbarger, used Claude to organize contracts, logistics, and experiments with 11 external labs, and delegated many other aspects of Mithril’s operations to Claude. As a result, Mithril took a possible treatment for one form of muscular dystrophy from an idea to promising results in mice in less than 18 months. Now at Anthropic, Cody is continuing this research, and plans to start several new programs. If his drug candidates continue to hold up, we expect a drug to be ready to start clinical trials in humans as soon as late 2028. Read more and see [our technical report](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/52e1f5d50c47ca3818f56704c27cf19e59b62e77.pdf).

## Extending our work in the life sciences

All of this research is still at an early stage. In particular, so far it is mostly _preclinical—_ that is, for the most part, it isn’t yet at the stage where the drugs are being tested in humans. We plan to continue extending Claude’s role into clinical trials as these drug programs advance, and as we partner with more organizations whose drug development programs are already at the clinical stage.

This research is only one part of our efforts to accelerate drug discovery. Ultimately, we want to share our models with as many drug development researchers as possible. To that end, we’ve rolled out [Claude Science](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-science-ai-workbench), our AI workbench for researchers, and we’re providing [Claude credits for life scientists](https://www.anthropic.com/news/ai-for-science-program). We’ve also created the [Life Sciences Verification Program](https://www.anthropic.com/news/life-sciences-verification-program) to allow trusted organizations to use our most powerful models with more permissive versions of our safeguards, which are necessary to prevent misuse but which can impede legitimate biological research. We’ve also recently launched an [open call for guest investigators](https://www.anthropic.com/news/open-call-guest-investigators-life-sciences) in the life sciences; we’re seeking proposals from research groups who want to use Claude to investigate key questions in drug discovery and other areas.

We’re looking forward to working with many more organizations as we expand our life sciences research. If you work at an organization focused on drug discovery and are interested in collaborating with us, you can get in touch below.

## Generate:Biomedicines: Redesigning a component of CAR T-cell therapy

_The Generate:Biomedicines team shares how they worked with Claude to redesign a component of CAR T-cell therapy to make it more compact, freeing up space for new functions that could help treat cancer._

_Read Generate’s [technical report](https://generatebiomedicines.com/publications/refactored-intracellular-domains-enhance-car-expression-and-function/) and get in touch (info@generatebiomedicines.com)._

[Generate:Biomedicines](https://generatebiomedicines.com/) designs protein drug candidates using machine learning and frontier biohardware. Over the past eight months, a six-person team of Generate scientists redesigned a stubborn component of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, a type of cancer therapy, with help from Claude.

CAR T-cell therapy uses genetically engineered versions of patients’ own immune cells to attack cancer cells. The part the Generate scientists redesigned is called the signaling domain—the section of the engineered receptor that tells the immune cell to attack. Making it shorter frees up space for other functions in the CAR’s genetic instructions, such as attacking several cancer markers at once or adding proteins that help the T-cell survive inside a tumor.

Working with Claude and other AI tools, Generate’s scientists built and directed a system of AI agents to design signaling domains that are much more compact than a standard version used in several approved therapies. The best design was about 70% shorter and no less effective. In laboratory tests, one of the top designs put roughly 10 times as much receptor on the cell surface—which may make a T-cell better able to recognize and attack cancer cells—and the lead designs killed tumor cells more efficiently than the standard version.

*   _Read Generate:Biomedicine’s technical report, “[Refactored intracellular domains enhance CAR expression and function](https://generatebiomedicines.com/publications/refactored-intracellular-domains-enhance-car-expression-and-function/).”_

### Why improving CAR T-cell therapy is a challenge

CAR T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of several blood cancers, but the drugs themselves are cumbersome to manufacture. Today, a patient’s T-cells are removed, engineered in a factory over several weeks, and infused back into the patient. A major goal for the field is to do that work _inside_ the body: delivering the genetic instructions for building the receptor directly to the patient’s T-cells. This could be a faster and cheaper way to deliver the therapy and could expand what CAR T-cell therapy can do. In particular, it could make the therapy better suited to treating autoimmune conditions, as well as early-stage solid tumor cancers, against which it has so far been less successful.

But delivering genetic instructions into a living cell means working within tight constraints. Space is at a premium: the instructions are typically delivered either by a viral vector or a lipid nanoparticle carrying mRNA, both of which can only hold a limited amount of genetic material. It would be helpful to give the CAR more functions, or to bundle in protective proteins to help the T-cell survive inside a tumor. The more compact each part of the receptor is, the more room is left in the delivery vehicle for these extra functions.

One way of boosting a CAR’s functionality would be to improve the delivery system—for example, by designing a capsule that can carry more genetic instructions. To use a software analogy, it would be like making a larger flash drive that can carry more information. But another way would be to make the individual parts of the CAR shorter—like writing software more efficiently so more program

Title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government

Markdown Content:
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.

We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.

Approximately 500 US federal, state, and local government organizations now use Claude. Weekly Claude for Government active users are up about eightfold since February, and usage across federal civilian agencies has grown about 20-fold in a year. Those organizations run some of the most important systems in the country, usually on tight budgets and with long procurement cycles. This agreement is built to support that work, so they can apply Claude to hard problems without a large upfront commitment.

The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.

### **How Claude is helping public servants get more done**

Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:

*   Utah gave Claude Code to 34 developers across 10 state agencies. 80% had a working environment within 30 minutes, 71% reported saving 20+ hours by the end of the four-week pilot.
*   A US state CIO confirmed their team was able to respond to a ransomware attack in 8 minutes vs. the usual 2-3 days thanks to Claude.
*   A US federal security team used Claude Mythos to detect and patch the vulnerability that would have allowed for the takeover of a critical production system in about two days. A human penetration test the month before had missed it.
*   A cybersecurity professional at a major agency found and patched bugs in critical financial systems.
*   A US state IT developer moved nearly 900 API methods to a new framework in two days. The project had been scoped for a month.
*   A US state IT director used Claude Code to document 12 legacy code repositories, mapping 467 database tables and flagging 27 risks along the way.
*   More than half of the US states, some of the largest localities, and some of the countries largest critical infrastructure operators [participated](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-cyber-mission) in our SLTT cyber defense program.

### **Meeting government security requirements**

Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made [generally available](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-for-government-is-now-generally-available) on September 30.

Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.

Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.

### **Getting started**

Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.

For more information, contact us [here](https://claude.com/solutions/government).

🚀 Mistral AI’s Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 ranks #2 out of 9 models by DER on Voice Arena’s Diarization + ASR leaderboard, outperforming its larger counterpart.

Following the launch of Mistral’s new Voxtral 3 family, we evaluated its Mini and Small transcription models on Voice Arena’s Diarization Bench.

🥈 Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3: 40.4% DER (#2)
Voxtral Small Transcribe 3: 41.1% DER (#4)

Both models were tested on 139 held-out conversations under identical conditions, using human-verified references, a strict 0 ms collar, and no predefined speaker counts or audio cleanup.

Mini leads on in-person conversations (40.6% vs. 41.5%), while Small performs slightly better on online calls (39.1% vs. 39.5%).

Overlapping speech remains the biggest challenge. Missed speech accounts for 82% of Mini's total DER. Both models correctly identify the exact number of speakers in 83.5% of sessions.

Congratulations to @MistralAI on the release ! 👏
